title: Feedback Architectures: Sprintseed Brief
body:
Purpose
Quick synthesis from CS field work (Aug–Sep 2026) to seed a sprint focused on runtime-facing feature requests and low-risk patches. Not an exhaustive plan; think of this as a compact playbook for eng + product pairing.

TL;DR
- Several mid-market customers report throughput regressions when using multi-turn chat with prefix caching and aggressive batching.
- Two recurring asks: (1) better visibility into KV cache eviction events and (2) a soft-degradation mode that reduces token-cost without breaking semantic continuity.
- Small wins: exposing a per-request cache-hint flag and adding a lightweight sampling metric for eviction hot-spots could unblock many customers quickly.

Raw signals & representative quotes
- "We see latency spikes every 15–20 minutes — it feels like some caches get flushed and requests go from 60ms to 700ms." — Customer A (fintech, dedicated)
- "When we enable aggressive batching, quality dips on follow-ups — the model loses context sometimes." — Customer B (marketplace, hosted)
- "We need an audit trail for what was served from cache vs recomputed — our compliance team keeps asking." — Customer C (healthcare, private)

Observed patterns (field detective notes)
- Spikes align with: autoscaler activity, model-variant fallback events, and maintenance window S3 eviction jobs. Correlation not causation but strong signal.
- Eviction behavior: customers on longer-seq workloads (avg 120 tokens/session) see more frequent KV churn. Short-seq apps less affected.
- Batching trade: high batch sizes improve throughput but expose model quality regressions on multi-turn prompts; customers are split on tolerable thresholds.

Prioritized wishlist (customer-facing language -> engineering intent)
1) KV-eviction observability (low lift)
   - What: per-tenant/per-model eviction counters + sample keys and approximate TTL traces surfaced in Console and via API.
   - Why: reduces time-to-detect; satisfies compliance asks.
   - Rough impact: high confidence to reduce CS-eng cycles by ~30% for top 10 customers.
   - Quick probe: add a flag to runtime: --eviction-sample-rate (default off); stream to telemetry backend.
   - Linked: INF-4782
2) Cache-hint header / request flag (very low lift)
   - What: allow caller to mark sections as cacheable: {prefer-cache | avoid-cache | bypass-cache}.
   - Why: gives app control; enables UX patterns like "system prompt only cached".
   - Quick probe: SDK + API header, no model changes.
3) Soft-degrade profile (medium lift)
   - What: a runtime profile that preferentially serves truncated KV contexts or lower-precision quantized variants when latency SLOs are jeopardized.
   - Why: keeps app online with graceful quality fallbacks; aligns with Dedicated SLAs.
   - Risks: requires careful rollback/telemetry and per-route config.
4) Eviction heatmap for Console (medium lift)
   - What: timeline visualization and hotspot table (tenant X model X node) showing eviction pressure.
   - Why: empowers SRE and accounts to pinpoint misbehaving sessions.

Suggested experiments for upcoming sprint (2-week cycles)
- Spike A (3 days): implement eviction-sample-rate with sampling at 0.1% for a handful of pilot customers; collect traces and compare to customer-reported events. Owner: Samir.
- Spike B (4 days): add cache-hint flag to API & SDK; instrument a/b with customers on hosted tier. Owner: Miguel.
- Spike C (7 days): prototype soft-degrade in staging using a) mocked truncated context, b) fallback to small quantized variant; measure quality delta on internal eval set. Owner: Evelyn + research.

Acceptance signals (how we know probes worked)
- Customer-facing: reduction in incident reports mentioning "sudden latency spikes" for participating accounts by >40% over 30 days.
- Engineering: eviction-sample-rate traces correlate with spike timestamps in >80% of pilot incidents.
- Product: no >10% measured quality regression for end-to-end user flows under soft-degrade (subjective QA + automated evals).

Unresolved questions / risks (notes to self)
- Sampling privacy: make sure eviction samples don't accidentally leak prompt contents. Store only meta keys + truncated fingerprints. Need legal sign-off.
- Cost: telemetry volume increase — estimate +3–7% egress for pilot customers. Finance ok? Need quick budget check (tag: INF-telemetry-budget).
- Rollout: avoid default-on for high-risk customers (healthcare, regulated). Provide per-tenant toggles.

Quick implementation checklist (minimal viable patch list)
- [ ] Runtime flag --eviction-sample-rate (default 0). (Samir)
- [ ] API/SDK header: X-Redwood-Cache-Hint. (Miguel)
- [ ] Console telemetry tile: eviction-counter + recent-sample-list (product + frontend). (Evelyn)
- [ ] Docs: short FAQ for account owners + compliance note. (Aisha)

Links referenced / tickets to open
- INF-4782: KV eviction metrics spike correlation (open)
- GH PR: runtime telemetry forwarding prototype (draft) https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/912
- Confluence seed: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/feedback-architectures

Next steps for CS & AE teams
- Offer pilot to 3 customers next week: fintech (dedicated), marketplace (hosted), healthcare (private). Emphasize opt-in.
- Prepare short one-pager for legal on sampling controls.
- Book 30-min sync with runtime eng + product next Wed. Agenda: confirm spike owners + measurement plan.

Notes to product reviewers
- This doc intentionally mixes customer quotes, assumptions, and rough engineering asks — use it as a conversation starter rather than a final spec.
- If we prioritize only one low-risk change first, make it cache-hint + SDK header. Fastest path to customer-perceived control.

Scratchpad (keep below)
- Measurement: add metric eviction_rate_per_minute and mean_rebuild_latency; tag by tenant.
- Slack thread: #cs-runtime-2026-09 has raw call notes.
- Potential follow-on: per-route "cache-sensitivity" analysis in Optimize to recommend cache-friendly prompt rewrites.

Revision history:
